nodes.title: Attempts that died before verification took 18.8% of measurable attempt-hours -- 4.30 of 22.91 hours, all scored zero, and none of them were waiting on the verifier
nodes.body:
Follows gap-w6-048 out of the exp-gap-005 measurement. In the era where verifier.finished exists (336 attempts from 2026-11-07T16:02 onward), 70 attempts never ran a verifier: 61 stopReason 'aborted', 9 with an error, all score 0. Their durationMs sums to 4.30 hours against 22.91 hours for the whole era -- 18.8% of attempt time, not 20.8% (the 20.8% was the attempt count; the two denominators differ because dead attempts are shorter on average: 221 s vs 245 s, though the difference is small enough that either number could be quoted and both are correct for their own denominator -- which is why both are printed).

What this is not: it is not verifier cost. A verifier run is 3.07 s mean (exp-ver-005), so the 266 that ran cost 13.6 minutes total, 1.0% of era attempt time. The 4.30 hours is agent time spent on attempts whose product was never scored.

What it could be, and the log can separate three of the four causes: 61 'aborted' without error means the parent stopped the child (a sibling won, or the round was cancelled) rather than the child failing; 9 'error' attempts have literal harness messages (the dispatcher disposed, described in w7-attribution). A fourth cause -- the attempt simply ran long and was replaced -- is not distinguishable today because attempt.deadline exists as a separate event and nothing joins it to attempt.finished by id.

Why it matters for the loop's economics: at the pooled 0.485 pass rate, 70 attempts are worth ~34 expected successes, and 34 successes at 25.2% promotion efficiency is ~8 promotions that were paid for and never saw a gate. The cash is not the issue ($0.0179 per attempt, so ~$1.25) -- the 4.3 hours are, because that is wall clock in which the loop could have been evaluating something that could have been promoted.

edges.note: gives the hours and the causal split the question asked for, leaving only the deadline join open
the 20.8% attempt share becomes 18.8% of attempt-hours; both denominators printed because they differ
9 of the 70 carry literal harness error strings and none were tagged infra at the time -- the label records silence, not harness failure
